title: Child Unaware of Data Collection
description: The child may not be informed about the extent of GPS data collection and its purposes.

title: Data Interception in Transit
description: GPS coordinates transmitted over the network could be intercepted by unauthorized parties.

title: Excessive Data Retention and Misuse
description: Backend may retain GPS data longer than necessary or use it for purposes beyond the original intent.

title: Tracking of Child's Movements
description: Aggregated GPS data allows tracking the child's location over time, enabling profiling.

title: Violation of Data Protection Regulations
description: Backend may not comply with legal requirements for handling children's location data.

title: Processing Location Data Without Valid Legal Basis
description: The backend processes and transmits location data without a clear legal basis (e.g., user consent or legitimate interest), violating data protection regulations.

title: Location Data Intercepted During Transmission
description: Location pings transmitted between backend and store may be intercepted if not encrypted, leading to unauthorized access.

title: Stored Location Data Linked to User Identity
description: Location history stored with identifiers allows linking data to specific users, compromising anonymity.

title: Secondary Use of Stored Location Data
description: Location data may be used for purposes beyond the original intent (e.g., profiling, advertising) without user consent.

title: Location Data Interception in Transit
description: Location pings transmitted between P1 and P2 may be intercepted if not encrypted, exposing sensitive user location data.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over unencrypted channels; no TLS/SSL protection.

title: User Identifiability via Location Data
description: Geofencing Engine may link location pings to specific user identities if identifiers are included in the data.
assumptions: Location pings contain user IDs or other identifying information.

title: Movement Tracking via Data Correlation
description: Correlating multiple location pings over time could enable tracking of user movement patterns.
assumptions: P2 retains and processes historical location data for analysis.

title: Excessive Data Retention
description: Location data may be stored longer than necessary for geofencing purposes, increasing exposure risk.
assumptions: No automated data deletion policies are enforced at P2.

title: Lack of User Consent for Data Sharing
description: Users may be unaware that their location data is shared with the Geofencing Engine.
assumptions: No explicit consent mechanism exists for this data flow.

title: Disclosure of zone definitions during transmission
description: Zone configuration data (e.g., home/school addresses) transmitted without encryption could be intercepted, exposing sensitive location information.
assumptions: Data in transit is not encrypted or protected by secure channels.
uncertainty_note: Tree node D.1.1 assumed based on standard LINDDUN Pro structure for data-in-transit disclosure threats.

title: Identifiability via zone configuration data
description: Zone definitions (e.g., home address) stored in P2 could be used to identify the user's residence or frequent locations if accessed by unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Zone data includes personally identifiable location information tied to user accounts.
uncertainty_note: Tree node I.1.1 inferred from LINDDUN Pro identifiability category; exact node may vary based on implementation details.

title: Unintended disclosure of precise location data
description: The Geofencing Engine may transmit more detailed location data than necessary (e.g., exact coordinates instead of zone entry/exit), leading to unnecessary disclosure of the child's location.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Notification data could be intercepted by unauthorized parties if the communication channel is not secured, exposing the child's location information.

title: Unauthorized use of location data by parent
description: Parent may use the received location data for purposes beyond the intended geofencing alerts, such as continuous tracking or sharing with third parties.

title: Linkability of child's location data
description: Location data from the geofencing engine could be linked with other datasets to build a comprehensive profile of the child's movements and habits.

title: Lack of child's awareness of data processing
description: The child may not be informed that their location data is being processed and shared with the parent via notifications, violating their right to be informed.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Processing location data without a valid legal basis or proper consent mechanisms may violate regulations like GDPR or COPPA.

title: Unauthorized access to stored data
description: Stored account, child profile, and geofence data may be accessed by unauthorized personnel, leading to misuse of sensitive information.
assumptions: Access controls on DS2 are not properly implemented or enforced.

title: Data breach due to inadequate security
description: Insufficient security measures on DS2 could result in unauthorized disclosure of sensitive data through breaches.
assumptions: Encryption and access controls are not adequately enforced on the datastore.

title: Non-compliance with data protection regulations
description: Storage of child-related data may not comply with legal requirements such as GDPR or COPPA regarding data retention and consent.
assumptions: Data retention policies and consent mechanisms are not aligned with applicable regulations.

title: Linking child profiles with geofence data
description: Combining child profiles and geofence zone data enables tracking of children's locations, increasing privacy risks through data correlation.
assumptions: Data is stored in a way that allows correlation between profiles and location zones.

title: Data interception during transmission
description: Data sent from P1 to DS2 may be intercepted if not encrypted in transit, leading to unauthorized disclosure.
assumptions: Transmission occurs over an unsecured or inadequately protected network channel.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Location history data transmitted between DS1 and P1 may be intercepted by unauthorized parties if not encrypted in transit.
assumptions: Assumes no end-to-end encryption is enforced for this data flow.

title: Unauthorized Secondary Use of Location Data
description: P1 may process or share location history for purposes beyond serving the parent's map/history view (e.g., analytics, third-party sharing).
assumptions: Assumes P1 has access to data beyond its intended scope without explicit consent.

title: Unauthorized Access at Destination
description: P1 may fail to enforce access controls, allowing unauthorized internal/external parties to view or extract location history data.
assumptions: Assumes P1 lacks robust role-based access controls or audit logging.

title: Parent unaware of data sharing implications
description: Parent may not fully understand the privacy risks of inviting another guardian to access child's location data.

title: Unencrypted invitation data transmission
description: Invitation data transmitted without encryption could be intercepted, allowing attackers to impersonate the parent and add unauthorized guardians.

title: Unauthorized access to guardian permissions
description: Stored guardian invitation data could be exposed in a breach, allowing attackers to gain unauthorized access to child's location.

title: Secondary data use
description: Backend may use guardian invitation data for analytics or marketing without explicit consent.

title: Insufficient Authentication of Secondary Guardian
description: The backend may not properly verify the identity of the secondary guardian before granting access, leading to unauthorized access to the child's location data.

title: Data Interception During Transmission
description: Live location data transmitted between the backend and secondary guardian may be intercepted if communication channels are not encrypted.

title: Unauthorized Data Sharing by Secondary Guardian
description: The secondary guardian may share or misuse the child's location data beyond the intended purpose without consent.

title: Lack of Transparency to Child
description: The child may not be informed that their live location is being shared with a secondary guardian, violating their right to awareness.

title: Lack of Audit Trail for Access
description: The backend may not log access events, preventing accountability for who accessed the child's location data and when.

title: Tracking of child's location over time
description: The child's manual check-in/SOS messages include location data that, when shared repeatedly, can be linked over time to track their movements. This could enable stalking or abuse by the parent or others with access to the data.
assumptions: The child sends multiple check-in messages over time, and the backend or parent retains historical location data.
uncertainty_note: LINDDUN Pro node L.1.2 ('Tracking over time') is inferred; exact node mapping may vary.

title: Eavesdropping on location data in transit
description: If the data flow is not encrypted, an attacker could intercept the child's location data during transmission between the child's device and the backend.
assumptions: The communication channel lacks end-to-end encryption or uses weak security protocols.

title: Unauthorized access to stored location data
description: If the backend stores the child's location data without proper access controls, unauthorized parties (e.g., malicious insiders, attackers) could access it.
assumptions: The backend retains location data beyond immediate processing needs and lacks robust access management.
uncertainty_note: Assumes the backend stores data; if it only relays data, this threat may not apply.
